method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, inductive-definition replay, stepwise reconstruction of all three displayed tableaux, and exact formula, macro, token and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The inductive construction and finite-tree definition of tableaux, open and closed branches, rule extension of existing tableaux, justification labels and a worked closure of true-signed A conjunction not-A.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Tableaux are generated inductively from assumptions and inference rules: the base case is one branch of one or more assumptions, and the extension case applies a rule to a branch of an existing tableau.
samples.checks: Both inductive cases and the one-or-more lower bound are explicit; the Marathi does not treat arbitrary trees as tableaux.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A tableau for n signed assumptions is a finite signed-formula tree whose n top entries are those assumptions in a vertical list and whose other entries follow correctly from an earlier signed formula on their branch. A branch is closed exactly when it contains both signs of one A; otherwise it is open. A tableau is closed exactly when all branches close, and open when at least one branch remains open.
samples.checks: The true/false sign alternatives, n assumptions, correct-rule requirement, biconditional branch criterion, every-branch closure and at-least-one open criterion are all retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An assumption set alone forms a tableau but normally is not closed; closure at that stage requires an opposite-signed pair already among the assumptions. Applying a rule to one occurrence of A extends every branch containing that occurrence.
samples.checks: The extension affects every relevant branch and only the selected occurrence's branches. The parenthetical is preserved as the source's necessary condition rather than silently rewritten as a new formal theorem.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Starting with true A-and-not-A, true conjunction adds true A and true not-A on one branch. Tableau annotations on the right identify the applied rule and source line. Applying true negation to line 3 adds false A, which pairs with true A and closes the branch.
samples.checks: All three tableau encodings, line references, truth signs, conjunction and negation rule labels, and the final close marker are source-identical.

source_observations: No source correction was required in this unit.
The definition distinguishes a closed branch from a closed tableau and requires all branches for the latter.
All tableau tree commands, formulas, rule annotations and close markers remain unchanged.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
वृक्ष, शाखा and टॅब्लो retain their established provisional status where exact Marathi specialist attestation is sparse.
The displayed tableau layout will receive visual inspection when the complete chapter enters the next cumulative reader.
